description:
All public `async fn ... -> Result<..., ClientError>` methods on SessionClient lack a `# Errors` rustdoc section. clippy::pedantic lints this (`missing_errors_doc`).

Affected methods (~17):
- src/methods/calendar.rs:18 (calendar_get), :45 (calendar_changes), :74 (calendar_set)
- src/methods/event.rs:18 (calendar_event_get), :58, :83, :126, :160
- src/methods/event_copy.rs:16 (calendar_event_copy)
- src/methods/event_notification.rs:12, :46, :80, :117, :151
- src/methods/participant_identity.rs:8, :36, :61

(event_parse.rs:13 and principal_availability.rs:14 already have # Errors sections — be consistent.)

Each method has slightly different error preconditions (empty id, empty since_state, empty token, missing primary account, malformed server response). Documenting each per method gives users:
- A grep target when they hit a ClientError variant they didn't expect
- A contract surface for future-self review

Pattern to copy from event_parse.rs:11-12:
```
/// # Errors
/// Returns `ClientError::InvalidArgument` if [field] is empty.
```

Plus one universal `Returns ClientError::InvalidSession` line for all of them (because session_parts() can fail for everyone). Plus the I/O error chain (Http, Parse, MethodError, etc.).
title: Public fallible methods missing # Errors rustdoc sections
